title: Romanticism & the Sublime
description: Nature at its most awe-inspiring, and the human drama set against it.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Distant View of Niagara Falls
items.description_narrative: Thomas Cole's Distant View of Niagara Falls, painted in 1830 with oil on wood panel, presents a sweeping vista of the iconic natural wonder. This work exemplifies Cole's profound engagement with the American landscape, often imbued with a sense of the sublime and picturesque.
items.tags: landscape, American art, romanticism, sublime, nature, Niagara Falls, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: New England Scenery
items.cultural_context: Hudson River School, American Romanticism, 19th Century American
items.description_narrative: Thomas Cole's 'New England Scenery' captures the wild grandeur of the American landscape. This 1839 oil on canvas work exemplifies the romantic vision of nature central to Cole's artistic output.
items.tags: landscape, american art, hudson river school, romanticism, 19th century, nature, sublime
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Pergola with Oranges
items.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: Thomas Fearnley's 'Pergola with Oranges' depicts a sun-drenched architectural structure adorned with citrus fruits. This oil painting on paper, later mounted on canvas, captures a serene moment through its vibrant depiction of light and nature.
items.tags: pergola, oranges, garden, romanticism, landscape, picturesque, vibrant
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Coming Squall (Nahant Beach with a Summer Shower)
items.cultural_context: Early American Landscape Painting, American Romanticism
items.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on cradled panel
items.description_narrative: This oil painting captures the dramatic moment of a summer squall approaching Nahant Beach, showcasing the powerful forces of nature. Dark, heavy clouds loom over an agitated sea, conveying the impending weather event with striking realism.
items.tags: landscape, seascape, storm, nature, romanticism, early american, dramatic
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/185185

items.title: Summit of the Sierras
items.medium: Gouache over graphite, on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: Thomas Moran's 'Summit of the Sierras' masterfully captures the rugged grandeur of the American West using gouache over graphite. This work vividly portrays the majestic peaks of the Sierra Nevada mountains, reflecting the sublime beauty of the natural landscape.
items.tags: landscape, american west, sierra nevada, mountains, gouache, romanticism, sublime
items.credit_line: Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Landscape with Dog
items.description_narrative: Thomas Doughty's "Landscape with Dog" depicts a serene natural scene, characteristic of early American landscape painting. Executed in oil on composition board in 1832, it invites contemplation of an untamed yet inviting wilderness.
items.tags: landscape, american landscape, nature, dog, serene, oil painting, romanticism
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/120081

items.title: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
items.description_narrative: Joseph Mallord William Turner’s "Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish" captures a dynamic maritime scene. The artwork showcases his distinctive use of light and atmosphere to depict the bustling activity surrounding fishing vessels.
items.tags: seascape, marine, romanticism, atmospheric, fishing, boats, 19th century
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Valley of Aosta: Snowstorm, Avalanche, and Thunderstorm
items.description_narrative: This dramatic oil painting by J.M.W. Turner captures the overwhelming power of nature within the rugged Alpine landscape of the Aosta Valley. The scene dynamically combines a snowstorm, an avalanche, and a thunderstorm, illustrating the sublime forces at play.
items.tags: romanticism, landscape, snowstorm, avalanche, thunderstorm, sublime, dramatic, nature
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
items.description_narrative: A quintessential piece of Romanticism. A man stands upon a rocky precipice with his back to the viewer, gazing out over a landscape covered in a thick sea of fog. It evokes a feeling of the sublime and the profound scale of nature.
items.tags: fog, mountains, romanticism, sublime, landscape, wanderer
items.credit_line: https://www.tiqets.com/ja/hamburg-attractions-c64886/tickets-for-hamburger-kunsthalle-skip-the-line-p976728/

items.title: Liberty Leading the People
items.description_narrative: Commemorating the July Revolution of 1830, the allegorical figure of Liberty strides over barricades and fallen fighters, holding the tricolour flag aloft. It combines the idealism of classical art with the gritty reality of modern war.
items.tags: revolution, liberty, flag, france, romanticism, battle
items.credit_line: Erich Lessing Culture and Fine Arts Archives via artsy.net

items.title: The Raft of the Medusa
items.description_narrative: Géricault based this monumental shipwreck scene on a real 1816 disaster in which survivors of the frigate Méduse drifted for thirteen days on a makeshift raft, resorting to starvation and mutiny. Its raw depiction of suffering and political scandal made it an inaugural masterpiece of French Romanticism.
items.tags: gericault, shipwreck, raft, romanticism, disaster, survival, french painting
items.credit_line: art database

items.title: The Nightmare
items.description_narrative: A goblin-like incubus crouches on the chest of a sleeping woman while a wild-eyed horse peers through the curtains, an unsettling image of dream and desire that scandalized and thrilled London audiences. Fuseli's proto-Romantic vision of the unconscious mind became one of the most reproduced images of its era.
items.tags: fuseli, nightmare, gothic, dream, incubus, romanticism, horror
items.credit_line: https://dia.org/collection/nightmare-45573 https://dia.widen.net/content/ecc0wgpx38/original/55.5.A-d1-2019-04-15.tif?u=u3bnol&download=true

items.title: The Hay Wain
items.description_narrative: Constable depicted a horse-drawn wagon fording the River Stour near his childhood home in Suffolk, capturing the changeable English sky and rural life with unprecedented naturalism. Poorly received in England at first, it won a gold medal in Paris and profoundly influenced French Romantic and Barbizon painters.
items.tags: constable, suffolk, countryside, river stour, romanticism, rural england
items.credit_line: https://en.gallerix.ru/album/National-Gallery-London-4/pic/glrx-1082704135

items.title: Rain, Steam and Speed - The Great Western Railway
items.description_narrative: A steam locomotive races across the Maidenhead railway bridge, dissolving into swirling rain and light in one of Turner's boldest meditations on modern industry overtaking nature. Its near-abstract handling of atmosphere anticipated Impressionism decades before the movement existed.
items.tags: turner, railway, steam locomotive, industrial age, romanticism, atmosphere
items.credit_line: http://www.artrenewal.org/pages/artwork.php?artworkid=14508&size=huge

items.title: The Fighting Temeraire
items.description_narrative: A grand old warship that fought at Trafalgar is towed by a small, sooty steam tug to be broken up for scrap, its ghostly white sails glowing against a blazing sunset. Turner's elegy for the age of sail mourns the passing of a heroic era before industrial modernity.
items.tags: turner, warship, trafalgar, sunset, romanticism, steam tug, british navy
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art

items.title: The Death of Sardanapalus
items.description_narrative: Inspired by Lord Byron's play, Delacroix depicted the legendary Assyrian king ordering the destruction of his possessions, concubines, and horses as his besieged palace burns around him. Its swirling composition and violent color scandalized critics at the 1827 Salon and it remains a landmark of French Romantic painting, held by the Louvre.
items.credit_line: GQEXB6lJVIn9wA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Women of Algiers in their Apartment
items.description_narrative: Painted after Delacroix visited North Africa in 1832, this interior scene of Algerian women at leisure was among the first Orientalist paintings by a European artist to depict a Muslim domestic space he had actually observed. It profoundly influenced later artists including Renoir, Matisse, and Picasso, and hangs in the Louvre.
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Cornfield
items.description_narrative: Constable depicted a boy pausing to drink from a stream on a lane through the Suffolk countryside near his childhood home, a scene combining closely observed nature with nostalgic sentiment. Presented to the National Gallery, London shortly after his death, it became one of the paintings most associated with his legacy.
items.credit_line: http://collection.imamuseum.org/artwork/56263/

items.title: The Charging Chasseur
items.description_narrative: Painted when Géricault was only twenty-one, this dynamic portrait of a mounted officer of Napoleon's Imperial Guard, rearing amid smoke and cannon fire, announced the arrival of French Romantic painting at the Salon of 1812. It hangs today in the Louvre.
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: The Combat of the Giaour and Hassan
items.description_narrative: Delacroix based this violent, swirling composition on a scene from Lord Byron's narrative poem 'The Giaour,' depicting a duel between a Christian avenger and a Turkish pasha. The painting exemplifies the Romantic fascination with literary drama, exotic settings, and dynamic movement.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Lion Hunt
items.description_narrative: Delacroix returned repeatedly to the subject of lion hunts late in his career, inspired by his 1832 trip to North Africa and by Rubens's earlier treatments of the theme. This turbulent composition of struggling men, horses, and lions survives as a fragment of a larger, partially destroyed canvas.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Friar Pedro Shoots El Maragato as His Horse Runs Off
items.description_narrative: This panel is one of six small paintings by Goya narrating the true story of a monk who overpowered and captured a notorious Spanish bandit, El Maragato, in 1806. The series' compressed, cinematic storytelling and stark realism anticipate the dramatic intensity of Goya's later work.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Peasants Bringing Home a Calf Born in the Fields
items.description_narrative: Millet painted this scene of French peasants carrying a newborn calf home from the fields, dignifying rural labor as a subject worthy of serious art. The painting reflects the Barbizon school's sympathetic focus on the everyday lives of the French peasantry.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Stoke-by-Nayland
items.description_narrative: John Constable's "Stoke-by-Nayland" depicts a familiar rural English landscape, rendered with his characteristic attention to natural light and atmospheric conditions. This oil on canvas masterwork captures the vastness of the Suffolk countryside under a dynamic sky, reflecting Constable's deep connection to his native region.
items.tags: landscape, romanticism, england, nature, rural, atmospheric, 19th century
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Alpine Scene
items.description_narrative: Gustave Doré's 'Alpine Scene' from 1865 captures the majestic beauty of mountainous landscapes through oil on canvas. This painting exemplifies his ability to render dramatic natural environments with intricate detail and atmospheric depth.
items.tags: landscape, alpine, mountains, oil painting, 19th century, romanticism, french, sublime
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/28146

items.title: The Storm
items.description_narrative: Pierre-Auguste Cot's 'The Storm,' created in 1880, captures a moment of dramatic intensity and emotional fervor. This oil on canvas masterpiece is a quintessential example of academic painting, renowned for its technical skill and evocative storytelling.
items.tags: academic art, French painting, 19th century, drama, romance, oil painting, figure painting
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: The Third of May 1808
items.description_narrative: Goya's iconic depiction of Spanish resistance fighters facing a French firing squad during the Peninsular War. Painted in 1814 to commemorate the Madrid uprising of May 2-3, 1808, it hangs in the Museo del Prado.
items.tags: Peninsular War, execution, Madrid uprising, Prado, history painting, Spanish Romanticism
items.credit_line: This file was derived from: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg:

items.title: The Burial of the Sardine
items.description_narrative: A small oil panel depicting a masked carnival procession that traditionally marks the end of Spain's pre-Lenten festivities. It belongs to a group of genre panels Goya painted for the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando in Madrid.
items.tags: carnival, festival, masks, genre scene, Real Academia, Madrid
items.credit_line: Mirar abajo.

items.title: The Doctor
items.description_narrative: A small genre panel showing a physician attending a patient, part of a set of cabinet paintings Goya produced early in his career. The work is held by the National Galleries of Scotland.
items.tags: genre scene, physician, cabinet painting, National Galleries of Scotland, everyday life
items.credit_line: National Galleries Scotland

items.title: Portrait of Doña Isabel de Porcel
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the Spanish noblewoman Isabel Lobo de Porcel, shown in a black mantilla in the maja fashion of the day. The painting is held in the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: portrait, mantilla, maja, Spanish nobility, National Gallery London
items.credit_line: http://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/paintings/francisco-de-goya-dona-isabel-de-porcel

items.title: Allegory of Love (Cupid and Psyche)
items.description_narrative: A mythological allegory traditionally identified with the story of Cupid and Psyche, though the exact subject remains debated among scholars. It is attributed to Goya's later mythological output.
items.tags: mythology, Cupid, Psyche, allegory, mythological painting
items.credit_line: WwE9WK44nrJhPg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Boy on a Ram
items.description_narrative: A tender genre scene of a child riding a ram, painted as one of a series of cabinet pictures for the Duke and Duchess of Osuna. It captures Goya's early interest in scenes of childhood.
items.tags: childhood, genre scene, Osuna commission, animals, 18th century
items.credit_line: ogHBX1jkH4Vu1g at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Students from the Pestalozzian Academy (fragment)
items.description_narrative: A surviving fragment of a larger composition depicting pupils of Madrid's Pestalozzian teaching academy. The piece is held at the Meadows Museum, Southern Methodist University.
items.tags: education, fragment, Meadows Museum, genre scene, children
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: Saint Gregory the Great, Pope
items.description_narrative: A devotional portrait of Pope Gregory I rendered in Goya's characteristic somber palette. The painting reflects Goya's religious commissions of the late 1790s.
items.tags: religious painting, pope, saint, devotional art, 18th century
items.credit_line: _QGADvU2Iz2-ug at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: A Woman and Two Children by a Fountain
items.description_narrative: A genre scene of a woman with two children gathered at a fountain, painted as part of Goya's series of tapestry-cartoon-related cabinet pictures. It reflects his early focus on everyday Spanish life.
items.tags: genre scene, fountain, family, everyday life, 18th century
items.credit_line: Colección Carmen Thyssen Bornemisza

items.title: Scene from the Inquisition
items.description_narrative: A small oil panel depicting a tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition seated before a group of condemned penitents. It belongs to a set of genre panels critical of Spanish institutions.
items.tags: Inquisition, tribunal, social critique, genre panel, Spanish history
items.credit_line: QAHsJoGPh6kFeQ at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: The Baptism of Christ
items.description_narrative: A religious oil sketch depicting John the Baptist baptizing Christ in the Jordan River. It is a preparatory modello associated with Goya's religious commissions.
items.tags: religious painting, baptism, Christ, modello, biblical scene

items.title: The Madhouse
items.description_narrative: A small oil panel showing inmates confined within an asylum courtyard, part of a series of genre panels Goya painted late in his career for the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. The work reflects his enduring interest in madness and social marginalization.
items.tags: asylum, madness, genre panel, Real Academia, social critique
items.credit_line: kwEoiMPuMB_17Q at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: The Bewitched Man
items.description_narrative: A scene from a comic play about superstition, showing a terrified man surrounded by braying donkeys he believes are demons. It is one of six paintings Goya produced illustrating scenes from popular Spanish theatre.
items.tags: theatre scene, superstition, donkeys, National Gallery London, satire
items.credit_line: Francisco Goya

items.title: Portrait of Miguel de Múzquiz y Goyeneche, Count of Gausa
items.description_narrative: A formal portrait of the Spanish statesman Miguel de Múzquiz, who served as Secretary of the Treasury under King Charles III. The sitter is shown in the dress and insignia befitting his ministerial rank.
items.tags: portrait, Spanish nobility, statesman, 18th century, court painting
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: Poetry and Poets
items.description_narrative: An allegorical composition evoking the muse of poetry among poets, held in the collection of the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm. It reflects Goya's later interest in literary and allegorical subjects.
items.tags: allegory, poetry, muses, Nationalmuseum Stockholm, literature
items.credit_line: Erik Cornelius / Nationalmuseum

items.title: Saint Isabel of Portugal Healing the Wounds of a Sick Woman
items.description_narrative: A devotional scene showing the sainted Portuguese queen tending the wounds of an ailing woman, an act of charity central to her legend. It was painted as part of Goya's religious commissions around 1800.
items.tags: religious painting, saint, charity, healing, devotional art
items.credit_line: -wEBwdqdiLnFhg at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Saint Hermenegild in Prison
items.description_narrative: A devotional depiction of the Visigothic prince Hermenegild, venerated as a martyr after his imprisonment and death for refusing to renounce his Catholic faith. The painting was likely produced as a companion to other saintly subjects from the same period.
items.tags: religious painting, saint, martyrdom, prison, devotional art
items.credit_line: ogE3xqulLmAntQ at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Time (Time and the Old Women)
items.description_narrative: An allegorical composition personifying Time alongside aging figures, reflecting Goya's darker meditations on mortality and vanity in his mature period. It exemplifies the somber, satirical tone of his later allegorical works.
items.tags: allegory, time, old age, vanity, mortality, satire
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — old-women-or-time-francisco-jose-de-goya-y-lucientes-1746-1828-lille-palais-des-beaux-arts/_wFNMfs3VQECBw

items.title: Monk Talking to an Old Woman
items.description_narrative: A genre scene depicting a friar in conversation with an elderly woman, rendered in Goya's loose, expressive late style. It reflects his continued fascination with everyday character studies in his final years.
items.tags: genre scene, monk, old age, character study, late style
items.credit_line: UwE-wr-m1D0h8Q at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Nantes, from the Île Feydeau
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Loire River tour, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner renders the quays and shipping of Nantes on the Loire in luminous, atmospheric washes, the town dissolving into golden haze along the water. Made during his tour of the Loire valley, it later informed engravings for his popular illustrated travel annuals.
items.tags: Turner, Loire, Nantes, France, river, harbor, watercolor, Romanticism
items.credit_line: https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/nantes-joseph-mallord-william-turner/yAEJ6OXlHp-DyA

items.title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, sublime history painting, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner witnessed the catastrophic 1834 fire that destroyed the old Palace of Westminster and translated the spectacle into a swirling vision of flame, smoke, and reflected light over the Thames. The painting exemplifies his late fascination with fire and dissolving form as vehicles for the Romantic sublime.
items.tags: Turner, fire, Parliament, London, Thames, disaster, sublime, night, oil painting
items.credit_line: Cleveland Museum of Art

items.title: Whalley Bridge and Abbey, Lancashire: Dyers Washing and Drying Cloth
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, topographical watercolor tradition, late 18th century
items.description_narrative: A young Turner records the ruined abbey and packhorse bridge at Whalley with cloth-dyers at work along the riverbank, blending picturesque ruin with everyday rural industry. The watercolor reflects his early career as a topographical draughtsman touring the English counties.
items.tags: Turner, Lancashire, Whalley Abbey, watercolor, ruins, river, picturesque
items.credit_line: Dordrechts Museum

items.title: Bonneville, Savoy, with Mont Blanc
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Alpine Grand Tour, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Painted after Turner's first Continental journey following the Peace of Amiens, this view of the Savoyard town of Bonneville sets peasant travelers against the distant, snow-capped bulk of Mont Blanc. It marks his early ambition to rival Claude and Poussin in grand Alpine landscape.
items.tags: Turner, Bonneville, Savoy, Mont Blanc, Alps, oil painting, landscape
items.credit_line: Dallas Museum of Art

items.title: Dort, or Dordrecht: The Dort Packet-Boat from Rotterdam Becalmed
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Dutch marine tradition, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A becalmed ferry and cluster of fishing boats sit motionless under a hazy golden sky on the River Maas at Dordrecht, Turner's homage to the seventeenth-century Dutch marine painter Aelbert Cuyp. The picture's still light and glassy water were praised in their day as a virtuoso demonstration of atmospheric painting.
items.tags: Turner, Dordrecht, Netherlands, marine, boats, Cuyp, oil painting, calm
items.credit_line: 4AFo7BatGeF12Q at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Lake, Petworth: Sunset, Fighting Bucks
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Petworth House series, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Painted for his patron Lord Egremont, this view of the lake at Petworth House dissolves the Sussex parkland into a glowing sunset haze, with two stags clashing in the foreground. It belongs to Turner's intimate series of Petworth landscapes celebrated for their poetic, almost abstract handling of light.
items.tags: Turner, Petworth, sunset, deer, parkland, lake, oil painting, Romanticism
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: The Red Rigi
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late Swiss watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Mount Rigi rises above Lake Lucerne, its rock face catching the deep red glow of sunset while the water below is rendered in near-abstract veils of color. One of Turner's most celebrated late watercolors, it shows him pushing landscape toward pure light and atmosphere.
items.tags: Turner, Rigi, Switzerland, Lake Lucerne, sunset, watercolor, Alps
items.credit_line: xwFy8KRlzdzvpw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Melrose Abbey
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Scottish Border antiquities, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner depicts the ruined Gothic tracery of Melrose Abbey in the Scottish Borders, a site made famous by Sir Walter Scott's poetry. The watercolor was made as an illustration for an engraved series on Scott's Border country, pairing architectural ruin with romantic literary association.
items.tags: Turner, Melrose, Scotland, abbey, ruins, watercolor, Walter Scott
items.credit_line: LwHVBTSigNIpIQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Queen Mab's Cave
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late imaginative landscape, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Inspired by Shakespeare's fairy queen from Romeo and Juliet, Turner conjures a dreamlike grotto of swirling color populated by tiny dancing figures. Exhibited in the final decade of his career, it shows the artist dissolving landscape into near-abstract fields of light and pigment.
items.tags: Turner, Queen Mab, fairy, fantasy, Shakespeare, oil painting, late style
items.credit_line: https://clevelandart.org/art/1916.1036 IA

items.title: Rockets and Blue Lights (Close at Hand) to Warn Steamboats of Shoal Water
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late marine painting, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: A paddle steamer fires warning flares through driving surf and spray to alert other vessels to dangerous shallows, the scene rendered in Turner's characteristic whirlwind of light and weather. The painting captures his fascination with modern steam technology confronting the raw power of the sea.
items.tags: Turner, steamboat, storm, sea, rockets, marine, oil painting, sublime
items.credit_line: https://www.clarkart.edu/ArtPiece/Detail/Rockets-and-Blue-Lights-(Close-at-Hand)-to-Warn-St

items.title: Llanthony Abbey, Monmouthshire
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, picturesque ruin watercolors, late 18th century
items.description_narrative: A young Turner captures the roofless nave of Llanthony Priory in the Welsh Black Mountains, tiny figures dwarfed beneath its towering Gothic arches. The watercolor typifies the 1790s vogue for picturesque monastic ruins that launched his early career.
items.tags: Turner, Llanthony Abbey, Wales, ruins, watercolor, picturesque, Gothic
items.credit_line: gAEk0hVZ9-6-Sg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Caligula's Palace and Bridge
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, imaginary classical landscape, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner invents a sunlit vision of an ancient Roman harbor and palace, loosely tied to the emperor Caligula's legendary bridge across the Bay of Baiae. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1831, it reflects his lifelong dialogue with the classical landscapes of Claude Lorrain.
items.tags: Turner, Rome, classical, Claude Lorrain, ruins, harbor, oil painting
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — xQFxUjK0z9Pb_Q Tate Images (http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00512&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1)

items.title: The Moselle Bridge, Coblenz
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Rhine and Moselle tour watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner depicts the old bridge over the Moselle at Koblenz where it meets the Rhine, boats and townsfolk small beneath a luminous evening sky. The watercolor comes from his later German river tours, prized for their jewel-like color and command of reflected light.
items.tags: Turner, Moselle, Coblenz, Rhine, Germany, bridge, watercolor
items.credit_line: RgFwkEDRp7lVFA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Dido Building Carthage
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, classical history landscape, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Queen Dido directs the construction of her new city of Carthage as the sun rises in blinding splendor over the harbor, a scene drawn from Virgil's Aeneid. Turner considered this his masterpiece and deliberately painted it as a direct rival to Claude Lorrain's classical seaport landscapes.
items.tags: Turner, Dido, Carthage, Virgil, classical, harbor, oil painting, sunrise
items.credit_line: J.M.W. Turner, Michael Bockemühl, Taschen (Köln), 1992, ISBN 3-8228-0669-2

items.title: Devil's Bridge, St Gotthard's Pass
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Alpine sublime, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Tiny travelers and mules cross the perilous stone span of the Teufelsbrücke as it clings to a sheer Alpine gorge, dwarfed by jagged peaks and plunging torrents. The watercolor grew out of Turner's 1802 Alpine tour, which supplied him with sublime mountain imagery for years afterward.
items.tags: Turner, Devil's Bridge, St Gotthard, Alps, Switzerland, watercolor, sublime
items.credit_line: 5AEUOFq9Jrulvg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Evening Landscape, with Castle and Bridge in Yorkshire
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Yorkshire patron commissions, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A ruined castle and stone bridge stand silhouetted against a warm, fading evening sky over a Yorkshire river, painted for one of Turner's northern patrons. The picture reflects his ongoing work in Yorkshire for collectors such as Walter Fawkes of Farnley Hall.
items.tags: Turner, Yorkshire, castle, bridge, evening, oil painting, landscape
items.credit_line: -gE2GV_i5hzang at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Calais Pier, with French Poissards Preparing for Sea: An English Packet Arriving
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, early marine painting, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner recreates the rough Channel crossing that greeted his own arrival in France, with fishwives and sailors battling wind and surf beside the pier while an English packet boat fights its way into harbor. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1803, it announced his ambition as a marine painter of stormy, dramatic weather.
items.tags: Turner, Calais, Channel, storm, pier, marine, oil painting, France
items.credit_line: https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/paintings/joseph-mallord-william-turner-calais-pier

items.title: Sun Rising through Vapour: Fishermen Cleaning and Selling Fish
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Dutch-inspired marine and genre painting, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A pale morning sun burns through mist over a fishing beach as figures sort and sell the catch beside moored boats, painted in homage to the calm Dutch marine scenes of Willem van de Velde. Turner so valued the picture that he requested it be hung beside a Claude Lorrain seaport in the National Gallery after his death.
items.tags: Turner, sunrise, fishermen, mist, coast, oil painting, Dutch influence
items.credit_line: The Yorck Project (2002) 10.000 Meisterwerke der Malerei (DVD-ROM), distributed by DIRECTMEDIA Publishing GmbH. ISBN: 3936122202.

items.title: What You Will!
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, literary fancy picture, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Figures in fanciful costume gather in a wooded park setting in this playful subject picture whose title borrows the alternate name of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night. It shows Turner experimenting with lighter, decorative genre subjects alongside his grander landscapes.
items.tags: Turner, Shakespeare, fancy picture, figures, park, oil painting
items.credit_line: Clark Art Institute

items.title: The Château de St. Michael, Bonneville, Savoy
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Alpine Grand Tour, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A companion view to Turner's other Bonneville picture, this composition places the fortified château against the same dramatic backdrop of the Savoy Alps. Painted after his 1802 Continental tour, it reflects his early effort to establish himself as a painter of grand Alpine scenery.
items.tags: Turner, Bonneville, Savoy, château, Alps, oil painting, France
items.credit_line: XgHfkn4uQCK_Dg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Lausanne: Sunset
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late Swiss tour watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: The rooftops and cathedral of Lausanne emerge from a haze of golden and violet light above Lake Geneva, painted during Turner's final decade of prolific Swiss travel. These late watercolors are prized as some of the most radically atmospheric work of his career.
items.tags: Turner, Lausanne, Switzerland, sunset, Lake Geneva, watercolor
items.credit_line: Wuselig

items.title: Tummel Bridge, Perthshire
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Scottish Highlands tour, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A stone bridge spans the River Tummel amid the wild hills of Perthshire, drawn from Turner's early tour of the Scottish Highlands. The watercolor shows his growing interest in rugged, untamed mountain scenery beyond the conventional English picturesque.
items.tags: Turner, Tummel, Perthshire, Scotland, Highlands, bridge, watercolor
items.credit_line: GQHBAgj90T1exA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Geneva, the Jura Mountains and Isle Rousseau, Sunset
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late Swiss tour watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Lake Geneva glows under a setting sun with the Jura range and the little Île Rousseau silhouetted in the distance, a subject tied to the memory of philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau. It belongs to Turner's late series of luminous Swiss lake views made for the dealer Thomas Griffith.
items.tags: Turner, Geneva, Switzerland, Jura Mountains, sunset, watercolor, lake
items.credit_line: Wuselig

items.title: The Sun of Venice Going to Sea
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late Venetian marine painting, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: A Venetian fishing boat named Sol di Venezia sets out at dawn, its painted sail catching the first light as the city dissolves into shimmering haze behind it. One of Turner's late Venice pictures, it exemplifies his mature dissolution of solid form into pure color and light.
items.tags: Turner, Venice, boat, sunrise, sea, oil painting, late style
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — dwEYd5yKW43wWQ Tate Images (http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00535&wwwflag=3&imagepos=5)

items.title: Panoramic View of the Thames
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, early topographical watercolor, late 18th century
items.description_narrative: A wide, calm sweep of the River Thames unfolds beneath an expansive English sky, an early example of Turner's topographical watercolor practice before his turn to grander Romantic subjects. The panoramic format reveals his precocious skill at composing broad, atmospheric river views.
items.tags: Turner, Thames, river, England, watercolor, panorama, early work
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: The Rainbow: Osterspai and Filsen
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Rhine tour watercolors, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: A rainbow arcs over the Rhine near the villages of Osterspai and Filsen, storm light and sun breaking together above the river and its vine-covered hills. The watercolor comes from Turner's 1817 Rhine tour, commissioned by his patron Walter Fawkes.
items.tags: Turner, Rhine, Germany, rainbow, river, watercolor, Fawkes
items.credit_line: pgEyeMCIVn7Bkg at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: East Cowes Castle, the Seat of J. Nash, Esq.: The Regatta Beating to Windward
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, yachting and marine painting, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Yachts race across the Solent before the turreted silhouette of East Cowes Castle, the Isle of Wight home of Turner's friend, the architect John Nash. The picture captures the fashionable sport of regatta sailing with Turner's characteristic dash of wind, spray, and shifting light.
items.tags: Turner, Cowes, Isle of Wight, yacht, regatta, sailing, oil painting
items.credit_line: Self-photographed, User:Daderot, April 2011

items.title: View off Margate, Evening
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late coastal watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Fishing vessels ride a calm evening sea off the Kent coast at Margate, a place Turner knew intimately from childhood visits and later years spent painting its ever-changing sky. The watercolor's soft, glowing tonality is characteristic of his late seaside studies.
items.tags: Turner, Margate, coast, evening, boats, watercolor, sea
items.credit_line: Clark Art Institute

items.title: The Schöllenen Gorge from the Devil's Bridge, Pass of St Gotthard
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late Swiss Alpine tour watercolors, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Sheer granite walls funnel a churning mountain torrent through the Schöllenen Gorge below the Devil's Bridge, one of the most dramatic passages on the St Gotthard route. Made during Turner's later Alpine travels, it revisits a site he had first sketched decades earlier with renewed painterly intensity.
items.tags: Turner, Schollenen Gorge, St Gotthard, Alps, Switzerland, watercolor, sublime
items.credit_line: Wuselig

items.title: Tours: Sunset, Looking Backwards
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Loire River tour watercolors, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: The city of Tours recedes along the Loire in a glowing haze of sunset color, the view looking back upstream as if from a departing boat. It is one of a series Turner made touring the Loire valley, later engraved for his illustrated travel annuals.
items.tags: Turner, Tours, Loire, France, sunset, river, watercolor
items.credit_line: SgG4AalnTq8YSQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Scarborough Town and Castle: Morning, Boys Catching Crabs
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, England and Wales coastal watercolors, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Boys hunt for crabs on the sands below Scarborough's clifftop castle as the morning light spreads across the Yorkshire coast. The watercolor was made for engraving in Turner's ambitious 'Picturesque Views in England and Wales' series documenting the nation's scenery.
items.tags: Turner, Scarborough, Yorkshire, coast, castle, children, watercolor
items.credit_line: MQEVP3xDJnjbeg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Kirkby Lonsdale Churchyard
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, topographical antiquarian illustration, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner frames the parish church of Kirkby Lonsdale through overhanging trees, small figures wandering among the churchyard's gravestones in soft northern light. The watercolor was made to illustrate Thomas Dunham Whitaker's history of Richmondshire in Yorkshire.
items.tags: Turner, Kirkby Lonsdale, churchyard, Yorkshire, watercolor, topography
items.credit_line: Bonhams London, 25 Jan 2012, lot 12

items.title: Bell Rock Lighthouse
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, maritime engineering subject, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Robert Stevenson's newly built lighthouse rises from stormy seas on the treacherous Bell Rock off the Scottish coast, waves crashing against its base under a turbulent sky. Turner was commissioned by Stevenson himself to commemorate the engineering feat in this dramatic maritime watercolor.
items.tags: Turner, Bell Rock, lighthouse, Scotland, storm, sea, watercolor
items.credit_line: LQEZojMomM-PzA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Evening of the Deluge
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, late color-theory series, mid-19th century
items.description_narrative: Animals and figures swirl toward an ark-like vessel beneath a darkening, storm-charged sky in this apocalyptic vision of the biblical flood. Painted as a pendant exploring Goethe's theory of color, it belongs to Turner's late series probing light, darkness, and moral allegory.
items.tags: Turner, Deluge, flood, biblical, apocalyptic, oil painting, late style
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Bass Rock
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Scottish coastal watercolors, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: The great volcanic island of the Bass Rock looms out of the Firth of Forth, seabirds wheeling above its cliffs and sailing vessels dwarfed beneath it. The watercolor was made for an engraved series on the antiquities and scenery of Scotland.
items.tags: Turner, Bass Rock, Scotland, Firth of Forth, coast, watercolor
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: Ancient Rome: Agrippina Landing with the Ashes of Germanicus
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, imaginary classical reconstruction, early 19th century
items.description_narrative: Turner reconstructs an idealized ancient Rome in golden light as Agrippina disembarks bearing the ashes of her husband Germanicus, a scene drawn from Tacitus. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1839, it reflects his ongoing rivalry with Claude Lorrain in monumental classical landscape.
items.tags: Turner, Ancient Rome, Agrippina, classical, history painting, oil painting
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — 6QEKBj-jyZHtOQ Tate Images (http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00523&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1)

items.title: Saint-Maurice, Valais
items.cultural_context: English Romanticism, Alpine tour watercolors, early-to-mid 19th century
items.description_narrative: The fortified bridge and gorge at Saint-Maurice, gateway to the Swiss canton of Valais, are rendered amid towering cliffs and a rushing river. The subject reflects Turner's repeated journeys through this narrow Alpine passage during his Swiss tours.
items.tags: Turner, Saint-Maurice, Valais, Switzerland, Alps, watercolor, bridge
items.credit_line: Unknown sourceUnknown source
